summary: This is a React dashboard that displays user feedback reactions (helpful/not helpful votes) aggregated by article. It requires admin authentication via a token, which can be provided through a URL hash, saved in browser storage, or entered manually. The dashboard shows summary statistics and a sortable table of reactions per article.

explanations.14: Object.entries converts the data object into an array of [key, value] pairs, so we can loop through each article's slug and its vote counts.
explanations.16: The ?? operator (nullish coalescing) provides a default value of 0 if helpful is null or undefined, ensuring we always work with a number.
explanations.19: We calculate what percentage of total votes were helpful; if there are zero votes, we default to 0% to avoid dividing by zero.
explanations.24: sort() reorders the rows: first by number of helpful votes (descending), then by total votes as a tiebreaker, so articles with more engagement appear first.
explanations.68: We use inline style with the ratio percentage to create a visual bar that fills from 0 to 100% based on the approval rate.
explanations.96: map() loops through each row object and destructures its properties so we can use helpful, notHelpful, etc. directly in the JSX.
explanations.143: preventDefault stops the form from doing a full page reload, which is the default browser behavior when you submit a form.
explanations.152: onChange updates the token state every time the user types a character in the password input field.
explanations.173: We construct the API endpoint by combining the site's base URL from Docusaurus config with the path to our reactions API.
explanations.185: This priority chain checks for a token in three places in order: first the URL hash (shared via link), then saved browser storage, then nothing — this determines the initial login state.
explanations.192: We return early if no token is provided, preventing an API call with an empty/invalid credential.
explanations.196: encodeURIComponent safely encodes the token for use in a URL so special characters don't break the query string.
explanations.197: A 403 status specifically means authentication failed (wrong token), so we clear storage and show a user-friendly error rather than a generic failure message.
explanations.213: [apiUrl] means this callback will be recreated if apiUrl changes, ensuring fetchData always uses the current API URL.
explanations.219: This effect acts as a listener — whenever token changes (from login, storage restore, or a hash link), it automatically fetches fresh data using that token.
explanations.224: We call fetchData directly here in addition to setToken because setToken is asynchronous and won't take effect immediately, so we fetch with the new token right away.
explanations.234: We only compute statistics (totals, percentages, sorting) if data exists; otherwise stats is null and we won't try to render the dashboard content.
